latest_nl_proof:
Let x be a real number and m a natural number. By compatibility of coercion with negation, we have (-(m : ℤ) : ℝ) = -((m : ℤ) : ℝ). Also, the natural number m viewed first as an integer and then as a real is the same real number as m viewed directly as a real, so ((m : ℤ) : ℝ) = (m : ℝ). Hence (-(m : ℤ) : ℝ) = -(m : ℝ). Therefore
x + (-(m : ℤ) : ℝ) = x + (-(m : ℝ)).
By the definition of subtraction in ℝ, x - (m : ℝ) = x + (-(m : ℝ)). Thus
x + (-(m : ℤ) : ℝ) = x - (m : ℝ),
as required. Since x and m were arbitrary, the statement holds for all real x and all natural m.
role_in_parent: Rewrites the negative branch so it can be fed into the negative-shift lemma.
statement_nl: For every real number x and every natural number m, x + (-(m : ℤ) : ℝ) = x - (m : ℝ).

domain_restrictions: m is a natural number and is coerced to a real number
negation is the additive inverse in the real numbers
subtraction x - (m as real) is interpreted as x + (additive inverse of m as real)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all real x and all natural m, x plus negative of (m as a real) equals x minus (m as a real).
quantifier_order: for all m in natural numbers
